limitations: These are original fictional training adaptations inspired by official public reports, not exact trial reconstructions. Each scenario subtitle and each exhibit carries that distinction.
No underlying judgment, contract, technical expert report, bank record or regulator case file was acquired. The four exhibits per scenario are authored teaching documents.
All published names, contact details and residential addresses were excluded. Scenario participants and organizations are fictional.
CON-02 is a regulator report about a court result, not the judgment. Its page date precedes the described judgment, so source.date is null; finality and appeal status remain unverified.

CON-14 source prints an inconsistent amount unit. The amount is not normalized into a verified fact; actual scenario calculation requires receipts. The two-delivery training chronology is fictional and must not be represented as the real record.
CON-08 source does not establish whether lessons had begun. The before-first-lesson setting is expressly fictional.
CON-13 publication date and image filename date differ; source uses the displayed article publication date and does not infer the incident date.

CON-08 and CON-09 are distinct Andijon course and Bukhara ATM incidents within one multi-incident article. CON-11 and CON-12 are distinct Andijon installation and Namangan visa-service incidents within another article. No republication was counted twice.
Source summaries are short original paraphrases. Aggregate source.summary text across scenarios sharing a URL stays below 120 words. No adolatzali.uz scenario or copy was used.
Law links were verified accessible, but case-date legal editions, procedural posture and remedies need educator/legal review before public release. All cases remain pending_educator_legal_review.
No API credentials, private systems or authenticated requests were used.

validation.referenceCheck: All option sourceIds refer to legalRefs IDs; evidenceIds refer to the case exhibits; all option scores are 0, 1 or 2.
